audit_sources.summary: Product Fitness work was still being wired through schemas, red fixtures, package inventory, and claim guards; the signal was that documentation-only Product Fitness was not enough.
The orchestrator was correcting stale proof, syncing installed/cache package version 0.0.10, and repairing red catalog/schema bookkeeping drift.
A proof blocker remained around live_registry_exposure and whether it was bounded reviewer-registry provenance or an overclaim of live app/marketplace proof.
The user typed the missing Chronicle/session-log audit request while the review packet lane was already active.
The packet lane produced source/install/cache evidence and a detached packet, but completed without a repo-owned session-log issue inventory.
Product Fitness ownership was missing as a first-class review disposition; generic Product/Simplicity approval could substitute for Product Fitness.
The user rejected a minimum Product Fitness ownership patch and required fail-closed first-class Product Fitness ownership with red fixtures.
Namespace/progressive-disclosure was identified as under-enforced and added as a first-class fail-closed requirement rather than documentation freshness.
A hostile review found same-version non-cache installed-root drift: installed audit had stale digest and lower red fixture count while source/cache were current.
The packet run loaded repo context and wrote review-packet-current.json, but the session-log audit request was not implemented as a repo-owned finding inventory.
The user added that this plugin must audit typed parsing boundaries, exact 100% coverage, and line-cap adherence because it is not exempt from Harness Ultragoal laws.
The packet summary recorded strict claim ceilings and no current live registry receipt, but remained outside the validator and did not include issue dispositions from session logs.

current_claim_ceiling: Supports only source-local session-log/Chronicle hardening inventory and fail-closed claim guards for the current source candidate. Does not support live app registry, Plugins UI, marketplace, install-button, launcher runtime, current reviewer exposure, material review sign-off, real user Product Fitness, daily-driver success, final packet correctness, install/cache parity, readiness, release, completion, update_goal eligibility, and does not support 100% coverage until each same-surface same-candidate receipt is regenerated and passes.

findings.affected_surface: review packet, validator provenance, package inventory
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Reviewer-ready, completion, and update_goal claims now depend on current same-candidate session-log hardening proof and cannot be inferred from a detached packet alone.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: A detached packet could look reviewer-ready without a repo-owned session-log/Chronicle issue inventory.
findings.observed_gap: The packet was created as a detached evidence bundle before the required June 25 Chronicle/session-log audit was turned into an issue inventory.
findings.required_repair: Bind session-log hardening to a schema, current package digest, required source ids, issue classes, finding row shape, validator check, and package inventory entries.

findings.affected_surface: active registry, material review, review packet claim ceiling
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: No live active-registry, Plugins UI, marketplace, install-button, launcher runtime, or current reviewer-exposure claim is supported.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Stale reviewer-registry or disk install/cache proof could be read as current Plugins UI, marketplace, install-button, launcher runtime, or reviewer exposure proof.
findings.observed_gap: A stale June 21 active-registry exposure receipt and local disk install/cache proof could be confused with current app registry, chooser, marketplace, or reviewer exposure proof.
findings.required_repair: Declare active_registry_current_proof as not_produced, require live same-surface registry observation for exposure claims, and keep registry/reviewer readiness out of the supported claim ceiling.

findings.affected_surface: source package, non-cache installed plugin, versioned cache package
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: No current install/cache parity claim is supported for this digest until those surfaces are refreshed and audited from the same candidate.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Same version string was allowed to obscure stale installed-root digest and lower red fixture count.
findings.observed_gap: Earlier same-version installed root proof had stale digest and fixture counts, so version 0.0.10 alone was not enough to prove source/install/cache alignment.
findings.required_repair: Block source/install/cache parity claims until source, installed, and cache receipts are regenerated from the same candidate digest after source compliance passes.

findings.affected_surface: Product Fitness schema, receipt, substitutions, validator
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: The proposal can support only package/static Product Fitness gate enforcement after current receipts are regenerated; it does not support real user Product Fitness or daily-driver success.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Documentation-only Product Fitness and adjacent install/smoke/package proofs could masquerade as product success.
findings.observed_gap: Product Fitness began as an added law and plan surface and needed enforcement against documentation-only proof and substitution claims.
findings.required_repair: Keep Product Fitness proof bound to schema validation, receipt digest/evidence checks, ownership/disposition checks, and substitution rejection checks.

findings.affected_surface: Product/Simplicity reviewer prompts, review-round schema, review fixtures, reports
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Product-impacting review claims are unsupported when Product Fitness disposition is missing, stale, unassigned, or substituted by generic Product/Simplicity approval.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Generic Product/Simplicity approval could substitute for a typed Product Fitness disposition with an assigned reviewer.
findings.observed_gap: Product Fitness ownership was not first-class in the review team and Product/Simplicity sign-off could stand in for Product Fitness.
findings.required_repair: Require Product Fitness ownership/disposition fields, assigned reviewer binding, freshness, and substitution red fixtures before product-impacting review claims pass.

findings.affected_surface: validator receipt, red fixture report, schema catalog
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Only regenerated same-candidate validator and red-fixture receipts can support source-local audit claims.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Generated schema bookkeeping and red fixture counts could drift while stale receipts still looked authoritative.
findings.observed_gap: Red catalog and generated schema bookkeeping drift changed expected fixture counts during the day.
findings.required_repair: Use current validator receipts with package digest, red fixture count, red report, runtime provenance, and package inventory closure instead of stale counts.

findings.affected_surface: review-round receipts, reviewer materiality, registry preflight
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Material review sign-off remains unsupported without fresh same-round reviewer exposure and live reviewer outputs.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Same-round reviewer-spawn provenance could be overread as broader app registry or marketplace proof.
findings.observed_gap: The review-round validator treats live_registry_exposure as same-round reviewer-spawn provenance, but that proof does not become app registry or marketplace proof.
findings.required_repair: Continue enforcing same-round exposure/session matching in review-round receipts and keep stronger app-registry claims out of the packet.

findings.affected_surface: agent standards enforcement, standards gardening, red fixtures
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Standards rows can support package/static enforcement only where current validator checks bind them to real checks, fixtures, and receipts.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Standards rows and zero-evidence fixtures could be treated as prose rather than proof-bearing enforcement.
findings.observed_gap: Session evidence repeatedly called out standards enforcement rows and zero-evidence red fixture work as proof-bearing, not prose-only.
findings.required_repair: Keep standards rows under validator-backed agent-standards-enforcement, source-obligation parity, and standards-gardener-promotion checks.

findings.affected_surface: validator JSON boundary, schema catalog, typed semantic receipt loaders
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Typed-boundary enforcement is supported only after current same-candidate tests and audit receipts pass; it does not cover untested runtime surfaces.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: The plugin could teach typed boundaries to target repos while failing to enforce them on its own validator and receipts.
findings.observed_gap: The plugin itself needed a current check that parsing and typed boundaries are real, not merely taught to generated target repos.
findings.required_repair: Run validator unit and package audits through json_boundary/schema_catalog paths and typed receipt checks for JSON parsing, schema resolution, path containment, symlink, hardlink, and stale digest fields.

findings.affected_surface: validator source coverage, completion/readiness/material sign-off claim ceiling
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: No 100% coverage, complete, ready, release, production, phase advancement, or material sign-off claim is supported until current coverage is regenerated for this digest.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: The plugin could claim Harness Ultragoal compliance without exact 100% self-coverage and uncovered_records = [].
findings.observed_gap: The repo previously had no root .harness/coverage-command and live cargo llvm-cov proof failed the 100% line coverage gate.
findings.required_repair: Do not claim complete, ready, release-ready, material sign-off, or 100% coverage until the current candidate has a typed coverage receipt proving coverage.percent = 100 with uncovered_records = [].

findings.claim_ceiling_impact: Line-cap adherence is source-local implementation evidence only and does not replace coverage, source audit, or live registry proof.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Validator hardening could create oversized source files while claiming compliance with the laws it enforces.
findings.observed_gap: The plugin source needed a current line-cap check against the active Rust migration hard cap of 250 lines unless generated or explicitly justified.
findings.required_repair: Keep changed Rust source under 250 lines and avoid broad line-cap exceptions; the session-log hardening move leaves changed Rust files at 239, 228, 51, 1, and 1 lines.

findings.affected_surface: validator source topology, package inventory, standards, source obligations, final packet claim ceiling
findings.claim_ceiling_impact: No completion, review, package, readiness, release, final packet, CLI self-law, or update_goal claim may pass while namespace/progressive-disclosure or source topology checks fail.
findings.observed_bad_behavior: Namespace/progressive-disclosure could be treated as documentation freshness or broad traceability instead of a first-class fail-closed law.
findings.observed_gap: Namespace/progressive-disclosure was called out as under-enforced and required dedicated standards rows, trace entries, validators, fixtures, receipts, and claim guards.
findings.required_repair: Keep namespace-progressive-disclosure and validator-source namespace topology under dedicated checks, red/green/tamper fixtures, package inventory closure, and claim guards.
